Sri Lanka, on the other hand, will not be happy with their effort as it many of their batters got starts but could not convert them. Nishan Madushka scored a fifty but never really looked settle and it was once again Dhananjaya de Silva who fought like a lone warrior for the hosts and at least gave their bowlers something to bowl about. DDS was the top-scorer 82 runs while Ramesh Mendis also chipped in with a well-made 42 which has helped them to set this target. However, they will need something really special from their bowlers to defend it.

131 IS THE TARGET FOR PAKISTAN! They were pretty good with the ball right from the start and it was their spinner who got the crucial breakthroughs in the middle. Nauman Ali started things off by getting rid of Dimuth Karunaratne and finished with three wickets while Abrar Ahmed supported him well with three as well. Agha Salman got two important wickets as well but they were not able to break through the defense of DDS who continued his good form. Their catching though was absolutely amazing which has been a key factor in this Test. However, after taking the second new ball, Shaheen Afridi removed him and wrapped up things for them.

SESSION SUMMARY - 116 runs and 3 wickets in 32 overs. A fine session of Test cricket! Both sides went hard at each other but at the moment Pakistan are a bit ahead in the game. Nishan Madushka got to his fifty but got out just after Lunch while Dhananjaya de Silva and Dinesh Chandimal steadied things for a bit. However, a brilliant catch from Imam-ul-Haq for rid of the latter on the bowling Agha Salman while Abdullah Shafique took a blinder at short leg to dismiss Sadeera Samarawickrama once again in a similar fashion as Salman picked up his second wicket. After that, DDS changed gears and started scoring at a quick rate and got good support from Ramesh Mendis too. He registered his fifty and helped the hosts take a lead of 61 runs, and everything now depends on how he manages with the tail-enders to set a decent target for the visitors. Pakistan, on the other hand, will look to quickly wrap up things in the next session and chase it down to win the Test as there is a lot of time left in this match. Join us at 3.30 pm IST (10 am GMT) to see how things pan out in the final session.

Shaheen Afridi bowled brilliantly finding the right spots in the morning but was unlucky as Nishan Madushka had the lady luck in his court with edges flying past the slip cordon for fun and for runs. Naseem Shah was a bit waivered and proved costly which enforced the bowling change early on as the skipper brought in Abrar Ahmed into the attack and it paid dividends with him picking up Dimuth Karunaratne while later in the session Nauman Ali got a couple of wickets as well. A make-or-break session awaits us on the other side of this lunch break which will start at 12.55 pm IST (7.25 am GMT).

The day started off on a really positive note for the hosts as they scored at a brisk pace and found the fence more often than not. Dimuth Karunaratne looked solid till he stayed while Nishan Madushka struggled a bit but got through the storm of Shaheen Afridi unscratched. The duo added 28 runs this morning in a little over 6 overs into the day when Dimuth Karunaratne departed to a stunning catch from Agha Salman. It was then Kusal Mendis that walked into the frame of schemes and stabled the ship with his sensible strokeplay ability along with Nishan Madushka but was later trapped in front of his stumps and lost his wicket. Closer to Lunch it was the experienced Angelo Mathews that departed to a splendid catch from Babar Azam edging one of the bowling of Nauman Ali. At Lunch the Lankan side would be slightly unhappy to have lost 3 wickets in the morning session but would be pleased to have managed to cut down the Pakistani lead to just 56 runs now.

Lunch has been called by the match officials and the session seems to be a shared one as Sri Lanka scored freely but Pakistan got rid of a dangerous-looking Dimuth Karunaratne and a couple more in the first session.

Commentary.Commentary: We are all set to begin Day 4! The two umpires make their way out to the middle followed by the Pakistan players. Dimuth Karunaratne and Nishan Madushka stride out to continue the batting for Sri Lanka. Agha Salman to complete his over. Also, due to the lost time, Lunch will be taken at 12.15 pm IST (6.45 am GMT) and Tea at 3.10 pm IST (9.40 am GMT).
Update - There is some water around the run-up area and the groundstaff is working to remove it. There will be an inspection at 9.50 am IST (4.20 am GMT), so there will be a delayed start.
Update - The word from the umpires is that play will start at 10 am IST (4.30 am GMT), so not much time lost. We will update about the revised session timings in a bit.

The surface has started to grip and turn and do it viciously too. The Pakistani spinners would come in handy in the second innings but the target for the Lankan side would be to post a total of more than 200 as they have got the spin attack to back it up. Day 4 promises to be a moving day and the team that wins this day would probably take a firmer grip on this game. Stay tuned as we head towards the start of play in a while.

Day 3 belonged completely to the visitors as the marathon innings of Saud Shakeel helped the visitors take a commanding lead against Sri Lanka. Naseem Shah played a good hand too yesterday as he played the perfect anchor to Saud Shakeel. The Pakistani bowlers would be wanting to run through the batting lineup of the hosts in a hurry as the condition would favor the pacers early on. A lot would depend on this pair of Dimuth Karunaratne and Nishan Madushka as they would have to negotiate the likes of Shaheen Afridi and Naseem Shah early on with the ball being relatively new.
Hello and welcome to all our viewers as we build up to Day 4 of this exciting encounter between two Asian giants in Sri Lanka and Pakistan.
...DAY 4, Session 1...

Right then, that is it from a pretty long Day 3 where Pakistan have taken control of this game and will look to make early inroads on Day 4 while the hosts will need their batters to step up big time. We are surely in for some exciting action on Day 4 which starts at 9.45 am IST (4.15 am GMT), but you can join us early for the build-up. Cheers!

Sri Lanka, on the other hand will be very disappointed with their bowling effort. This is a ground where their spinner has a lot to say but that was not the case here. They were not able to pick up wickets at regular intervals and let the visitors get away. It was the same old story for them as they struggled to get through the lower middle order as the last five wickets for Pakistan cost them 360 runs which is a lot. Their catching was poor as well as they dropped Saud Shakeel twice which has made a big impact in this Test. However, Ramesh Mendis was the pick of the bowlers and took a five-for as they managed to bowl out visitors in the last session. Dimuth Karunaratne and Nishan Madushka had to see out a few tricky overs which they did without any damage.

Pakistan started the Day with Agha Salman and Saud Shakeel at the crease after ending Day 2 with a crucial partnership. They extended it further and at a good rate as well. Shakeel registered a fine hundred but they lost Salman in the same over who missed out on his century. However, that did not affect Shakeel one bit as he went on to build up two more big stands, one with Nauman Ali of 52 runs and then a huge one of 94 with Naseem Shah who showed great resistance which put the hosts on the back foot as they conceded a massive lead. Shakeel batted almost throughout the Day and completed his maiden double-hundred as well.

That's it for Day 3! The umpires have decided to call it off due to bad light but we got plenty of action and drama here. It ends with complete dominance from Pakistan! It is often called the 'Moving Day' in a Test match and this game has moved in favour of Pakistan massively now thanks to a magnificent 200 from Saud Shakeel. Session Summary - 86 runs and 2 wickets in 30 overs. The visitors have a good lead of 135 runs and are much ahead in this game with a lot of time still left in this Test.
